gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a base-M4 MacBook Pro (Thunderbolt 4, 40 Gb/s) a $149–$232 Thunderbolt 5 enclosure reads 1 TB in the same 4 min 23 s as a $54.90 USB4 enclosure, while on an M4 Pro/Max the measured gain is only about 1 min 36 s to 1 min 49 s per TB read, and the ORICO X50 Pro's measured 3,000 MB/s write on a TB5 Mac makes a 1 TB write take 5 min 33 s, slower than the TB4 rung.
standout_why: Cited rivals: the two ACASIS product pages list prices and 80Gbps claims but no time or per-port figures; DPReview gives ratios (1.2–1.8x) with no MB/s, no prices and no timings; OWC's blog gives MB/s per interface but no prices or copy times. Uncited picklog.cc already derives $/GB/s and 1 TB time, but only from claimed speeds and Sept-2026 prices, with no base-M4 case, no write-side figures and no DIY-vs-prebuilt cost per TB. Nothing in the result set puts today's prices against measured reads and writes or against the base M4's 40 Gb/s cap.
decides: Confirms 'no' for a base M4 MacBook Pro: every TB5 enclosure runs at the 3,800 MB/s TB4 rung there, so the $94–$177 premium over a $54.90 USB4 enclosure buys zero seconds. For M4 Pro/Max it narrows the pick: OWC Express 1M2 80G (6,000/5,500 measured) and UGREEN fanless (6,511/6,001 measured) deliver the TB5 gain on both reads and writes, while the ORICO X50 Pro's measured 3,000 MB/s write on a TB5 Mac is no better than USB4 for card offloads. It also undercuts ChatGPT's 'add a 990 Pro' advice: at Samsung's $639.99 for 2 TB, enclosure + drive costs $839.98 versus $749.99 for OWC's own prebuilt 1M2 80G 2 TB.
